surface_mechanism_description: The initial surface reaction involves displacement of a sec-butylacetamidinate ligand from a surface -OH group, forming a Si-O-Cu-(sBu-amd) surface species. Subsequent H2 exposure dissociates the ligands bound to surface Cu, releasing free amidine vapor and allowing Cu atoms to agglomerate. Ligand rearrangement from a bridging to a monodentate structure occurs through hydrogenation by surface hydroxyl groups above 220 /C176C, and this process is temperature-dependent.
evidence: The initial surface reaction of [Cu(sBu-amd)]2 with hydroxylated SiO2 takes place by displacement of one of the sec-butylacetamidinate ligands at a surface -OH site, thus forming a Si-O-Cu-(sBu-amd) surface species. Molecular hydrogen exposure during a subsequent pulse dissociates most of the sec-butylacetamidinate ligands bound to surface Cu, which releases free amidine vapor, leaving Cu atoms free to agglomerate on the surface. The thermally activated ligand rearrangement from a bridging to a monodentate structure occurs above 220 /C176C through hydrogenation of the ligand by surface hydroxyl groups after exposure to a [Cu(sBu-amd)]2 pulse.
